name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Castro holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage
District's D+16 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Incumbent seeking reelection after securing renomination
No public polls or expert ratings, leaving limited independent evidence
model.rationale: Joaquin Castro combines incumbency, a heavily Democratic D+16 seat, and a fundraising edge of about ten to one over Edgardo Rafael Baez, who shows minimal resources and no outside support. With markets pricing his win odds near 97% and no contrary evidence, this is a Safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any late polling, outside spending, or unexpected Republican mobilization in San Antonio would be the signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-20 is a heavily Democratic San Antonio-area district with a partisan lean of roughly 16 points toward Democrats. Joaquin Castro, the incumbent, is running for another term after securing renomination, and he holds a large financial advantage, having raised about ten times more than Republican Edgardo Rafael Baez, who entered the general election with modest cash on hand and no outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on the district's strong Democratic lean, Castro's incumbency and fundraising edge, and prediction markets that price his chances near 97%. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of recent polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
